reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only describes room-temperature tribology of CoCrFeMnNi (not CoCrFeNi) and does not involve FSP, nanocrystalline layers, or high-temperature behavior. It shows that a fine-grained sample (FG) has lower friction and wear due to an oxide layer, but this is under high load at room temperature, not across a temperature range up to 800 °C. The key premises about FSP, nanocrystalline structure, high-temperature oxide glaze, and hardness-mediated wear reduction are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: FSP refines grain structure and induces a nanocrystalline surface layer in CoCrFeNi
Nanocrystalline layer promotes in-situ formation of a continuous, self-healing oxide glaze during sliding
Oxide glaze acts as a lubricious and protective layer, reducing friction and wear from RT to 800 °C
FSP-induced grain refinement increases surface hardness, reducing plastic deformation and wear
Fine-grained (FG) structure yields more rupture-resistant oxide layer and lower wear rate
